clue.text: Dismiss objection from the old brass

definitions.note: the definition names a single instrument by its family, an early brass instrument

parts.note: to dismiss someone from a job is to sack them
a 'but' is an objection, as in 'no ifs or buts'

explanation.surface: A bandleader rejects a complaint from the old brass section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass' tempts you towards money or senior officers; here it is a family of musical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance forerunner of the trombone, an obsolete brass instrument.

clue.text: Plant that's said to open

definitions.meaning: an oil-seed herb grown in hot countries
in the Ali Baba tale the robbers' cave opens when the magic password is spoken

explanation.definitionFit: Sesame is a seed-bearing herb, and 'Open sesame' is the spoken charm that opens the cave in the Arabian Nights.

clue.text: Whacker's retiring without pension

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: a retiring person is shy, or coy
a rod is something you whack people with

explanation.surface: Someone who beats people is too shy to claim a pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like a hint about pensions but is the adjective meaning shy; 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A corody was a medieval allowance of food and lodging granted by a monastery, effectively a pension.

clue.text: "U B4 LA"? The decryption gives "soak"

indicators.note: decoding a cipher means sorting jumbled letters back into the right order

parts.note: read as letters: U, four Bs, L and A
taken as written

explanation.surface: A text-speak code is cracked to reveal the word 'soak'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'B4' looks like text-speak for 'before', but it means B four times. With U, L, A and THE that gives the ten letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A long relaxing soak in a tub of foamy water is exactly what this kind of bath offers.

clue.text: Jobs for many in erstwhile news agency

indicators.note: the letter for many is placed inside the agency's name

parts.note: TASS was the official news agency of the Soviet Union
K, short for a thousand, stands for a large number

explanation.surface: Work assignments for lots of staff at a defunct news agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, which is what jobs are in this sense.

clue.text: Turned frying pan on bird in part of China

indicators.note: the cooking pan's name is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese frying pan
the loon is a diving bird, the North American name for a diver

explanation.surface: Someone flips a frying pan over a bird in a Chinese kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' suggests tossing food, but it reverses WOK to give KOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Kowloon is the peninsula of Hong Kong facing the island across the harbour.

clue.text: 'twas blown as gloom lifted from hearts ere noon

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the word reads it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: murk is gloom or darkness

indicators.note: the setter uses this loosely to bring the letter for hearts into the morning word

parts.note: before noon is the morning, or morn
H is the card-playing abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: An old tune played as spirits lifted before midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifted' turns the gloom word upwards, as befits a down clue; 'from' is only a loose signal for putting the hearts letter inside the morning word.
explanation.definitionFit: The krummhorn is a Renaissance wind instrument, now obsolete, hence 'twas blown in the past tense.

clue.text: Cried for Soppy Party's leader to be introduced

indicators.note: the first letter goes into the middle of the word for soppy

parts.note: soppy or feeble people are called wet in British slang

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone cried because a feeble party's leader was being presented.
explanation.definitionFit: Wept is the past tense of weep, meaning cried tears.

clue.text: Remove regulation restricting officer's beat

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hem in the abbreviation for officer
regulating something puts it into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer

explanation.surface: Get rid of the rule that limits an officer's patrol route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like a police patrol; it is the verb meaning defeat. 'Regulation' rearranges REMOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcome an opponent is to defeat or beat them.

clue.text: Boycotting garments made from disembowelled ruminants

indicators.note: the answer is made by reworking these letters into a new order
the middle letter, the innards of the word, is cut out

explanation.surface: A protest against clothing made from the guts of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disembowelled' drops the central N of RUMINANTS; the remaining eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturism is the practice of going without clothes, here wittily framed as refusing to wear them.

clue.text: Plant an hour in advance

indicators.note: the abbreviation for hour is placed inside the word for advance

parts.note: a sub is an advance payment of wages

explanation.surface: Get something in the ground an hour early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a verb; it is the noun defined. 'Advance' is a sub, an advance on wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrub is a woody bush, one kind of plant.

clue.text: Concrete assessment of politician's setback, ensnared by loose woman

indicators.note: the first pieces are trapped inside the word for loose woman

parts.note: a derogatory word for a promiscuous woman
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: the word set is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician's setback, caught up with a woman of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setback' looks like one word meaning reverse, but the setter splits it: 'back' turns 'set' round.
explanation.definitionFit: A slump test measures the workability of fresh concrete by how far a cone of it sags.

clue.text: Intrusive old Iranian adopting new models

indicators.note: the ancient people's name takes in the other letters

parts.note: the Medes were an ancient people of what is now Iran

indicators.note: a new version of the word models, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A nosy ancient Persian takes on some fresh models.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddlesome person interferes in others' business, which is to be intrusive.

clue.text: Not a pretty sight from hill and river

definitions.meaning: a mark left on the skin after a wound has healed
a steep rocky outcrop on a hillside, as in the Yorkshire Dales
a river of that name, such as ... Water in Dumfriesshire

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a healed wound's mark, and also names a rocky hill cliff in northern England.

clue.text: Chirpy bloke at sea, not grand, but overstated

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, K

explanation.surface: A cheery fellow on a ship, not impressive but exaggerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not grand' means CHIRPY BLOKE loses K before 'at sea' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbolic language exaggerates, so it is overstated.

clue.text: Expression of gut feelings about grubby rooms

indicators.note: the letters move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone voices instinctive disgust at squalid accommodation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gut feelings' suggests intuition but literally means the stomach rumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Borborygmus is the medical name for the rumbling noise of gas moving through the intestines.

clue.text: Translation of "coat"

definitions.meaning: a version of a text in another language
a layer of plaster or cement applied to a wall

explanation.definitionFit: A rendering is a translation or interpretation, and also a coat of plaster on a wall.

clue.text: Song's opening's memorable: "King's caught in grating"

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the letter for king is held inside the word for memorable

parts.note: a catchy tune sticks in the memory
R is the abbreviation for Rex, king

explanation.surface: A review praising a song's catchy start, quoting a line about a king behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grating' in the surface is a set of bars; as the definition it is the adjective for a harsh sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A scratchy sound is rough and harsh, as a grating noise is.

clue.text: Sudden appearance of bishop in shocking state

indicators.note: the letter for bishop goes inside the word for shocking

parts.note: outré means unconventional to the point of shocking
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
AK is the postal abbreviation for Alaska, a US state

explanation.surface: A bishop's sudden arrival in a scandalous condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking state' reads as one phrase, but it is two pieces: OUTRE and the US state AK.
explanation.definitionFit: An outbreak is the sudden start of something such as a disease or war.

clue.text: Face sanction

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a face and a verb for tolerating or approving.

clue.text: Allied triumph in clay is something amazing

indicators.note: the victory letters go inside the word for clay

parts.note: marl is a clay-rich soil
VE Day marked the Allied victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: An Allied victory set in clay makes a wonderful sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A marvel is a wonder, something astonishing.

clue.text: Hotchpotch produced by sealine of sorts?

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
a ley is a supposed alignment of ancient sites, a ley line

explanation.surface: A jumble produced by some kind of coastal line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sealine' splits into 'sea' and 'line'; 'of sorts' warns that this is an odd way to read them.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a varied mixture, as a hotchpotch is.

clue.text: Like smell of theoretical yob-stopper?

definitions.note: the definition names a British court order meant to curb loutish behaviour

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: Something that smells bad is supposed to deter hooligans.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order; 'theoretical' teases that it often failed to stop yobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anti-Social Behaviour Order was a UK civil order aimed at curbing loutish conduct.

clue.text: Cleric backing child support without fish or fowl, say

indicators.note: the clergyman's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, wrapping the support round the child

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
a brat is a child, usually badly behaved

explanation.surface: A clergyman supports a child, but not with fish or poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without fish or fowl' looks like a diet, but 'without' means outside, and 'fish or fowl, say' is a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish and birds both have backbones, so each is an example of this class of animal.

clue.text: Article about compiler by female felon

indicators.note: the article goes round the letter for the compiler

parts.note: the is the definite article
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the setter and a woman criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief commits theft, a crime, so is a felon.

clue.text: Supposing America turned mystic

indicators.note: the two words together are turned round to read backwards

parts.note: if means supposing
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Imagine that America became mystical.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a follower of the mystical tradition within Islam.

clue.text: Composer fomenting revolutionary friction in Italy

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born revolutionary
a rub is friction
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A composer stirring up a revolutionary's quarrel in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fomenting' links the definition to the wordplay, which spells out the name piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Cherubini was an Italian composer of operas and sacred music, active in Paris.

clue.text: Balanced, from both points of view

indicators.note: a word that reads the same whichever end you start from

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A fair verdict that sees both sides of the argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From both points of view' sounds like fairness but means the word reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something level is even, with neither side higher, so balanced.

clue.text: Vacuous discourse from leader of oxen?

parts.note: the yak is a long-haired ox of Tibet
a king is a leader

explanation.surface: Empty chatter from the chief of a herd of cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of oxen' is read the other way round: a king of the yaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Yakking is incessant trivial chatter, idle and empty talk.

clue.text: Not working to recruit head of chemistry department

indicators.note: the broken word takes on a new member, a letter placed inside it

parts.note: something faulty is not working

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A broken-down university hires someone to lead chemistry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of chemistry' looks like a job title; it gives just C.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a division of a university, a department or group of them.
